edges.description: Shows that ADAMTS18 is required for lens-capsule integrity during rapid embryonic lens growth.
edges.limitations: The mouse eye phenotype is restricted to the posterior lens capsule. The mice do not reproduce microcornea, anterior segment dysgenesis or myopia, and their retina is structurally and functionally normal.

edges.description: The knockout retina is structurally normal with a preserved electroretinogram.
edges.limitations: Mouse eyes are not myopic and lack a macula, so the human retinal and chorioretinal phenotype may depend on features the mouse eye does not have. This is a hypothesis; it has not been tested.
Transient developmental morpholino knockdown in a fish, not a stable loss-of-function allele in a mammalian eye; the chorioretinal atrophy and anterior segment features are not modelled.

evidence.reference_title: The syndrome of microcornea, myopic chorioretinal atrophy, and telecanthus (MMCAT) is caused by mutations in ADAMTS18.
evidence.snippet: Reassuringly, the autozygomes of all probands overlap on the same chr16q23.1 locus, further supporting the positional mapping of MMCAT to ADAMTS18.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of ADAMTS18 as a gene mutated in Knobloch syndrome.
evidence.snippet: By filtering variants generated on exome sequencing using runs of autozygosity in this simplex case, the study identified ADAMTS18 as the only gene carrying a homozygous protein altering mutation.

evidence.reference_title: Expansion of genotypic and phenotypic findings in ADAMTS18-related ocular pathology.
evidence.snippet: Initially, these cases were undifferentiated from Knobloch syndrome but genetic testing as well as phenotypic findings separated it from autosomal recessive Knobloch syndrome.

nodes.description: Viable Adamts18-null mice with a fully penetrant posterior lens-capsule defect from embryonic day 13.5, with extrusion of lens fibre cells into the vitreous; retinal structure and electroretinogram are normal. The mice also have altered bronchiolar branching and female reproductive tract defects.

Developmental anomalies of the anterior eye: small corneas, displaced and small pupils, posterior embryotoxon, abnormal iridocorneal angle development, and lens anomalies including childhood cataract, ectopia lentis and a small spherical lens. Angle anomalies can cause developmental glaucoma. The pattern resembles Axenfeld-Rieger spectrum but is recessive and lacks the extraocular disease of FOXC1 and PITX2 disorders.

evidence.reference_title: ADAMTS18-related anterior segment dysgenesis mistaken as Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Microcornea with myopic chorioretinal atrophy, a less common ASD, is distinct, recognizable, and secondary to biallelic pathogenic variants in the metalloproteinase gene ADAMTS18.

evidence.reference_title: Expansion of ocular phenotypic features associated with mutations in ADAMTS18.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in ADAMTS18 are associated with ocular developmental abnormalities including microcornea, ectopia lentis, and early onset of cone-rod dystrophy.

nodes.description: Biallelic ADAMTS18 variants, including nonsense alleles (p.Leu356*, p.Gly467*, p.Cys686*, p.Arg1047*) that are expected to remove the protein and missense alleles that cluster in the cysteine-rich and thrombospondin-repeat ancillary domains. Loss of function is inferred from the nonsense alleles and from the recessive inheritance; no patient allele has been tested for catalytic activity.

evidence.snippet: Direct sequencing of this gene in four additional probands with the same phenotype revealed three additional homozygous changes in ADAMTS18 including two nonsense mutations.

evidence.snippet: The clinical diagnosis was bilateral developmental glaucoma with microcornea.

nodes.description: ADAMTS18 is expressed in the developing lens, surface ectoderm, prospective cornea and optic cup, and later in the inner retina. Loss of its activity is thought to disturb extracellular matrix remodeling as these tissues grow. In Adamts18-null mice the only eye defect is a posterior lens-capsule failure that appears at embryonic day 13.5, when the lens grows rapidly, with herniation of lens fibre cells into the vitreous. How the same loss produces small corneas, angle anomalies and retinal degeneration in humans is unresolved (see discussions).

nodes.description: ADAMTS18 is a secreted zinc-dependent metalloproteinase that acts on extracellular matrix. Its one well-characterised substrate is fibronectin: it cleaves fibronectin in the linker between type I modules 5 and 6, removing the N-terminal fragment that fibronectin needs to assemble into fibrils, and its loss leads to fibronectin accumulation in knockout tissues. Whether fibronectin is the substrate that matters in the eye is not known.

evidence.reference_title: A disintegrin and metalloproteinase with thrombospondin motifs 18 (ADAMTS18) cleaves fibronectin and negatively regulates its fibrillogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Using mass spectrometry, we identified two sites in FN that are proteolytically cleaved by ADAMTS18, including a cleavage site in the linker FN-I5-6.

evidence.reference_title: A disintegrin and metalloproteinase with thrombospondin motifs 18 (ADAMTS18) cleaves fibronectin and negatively regulates its fibrillogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Knockout of ADAMTS18, either in mouse models or in vitro, was shown to lead to FN accumulation, mutation in epithelial branching, and reduction in endothelial sprouting.

nodes.description: Morpholino knockdown of the medaka orthologue impairs photoreceptor function and supported the pathogenicity of a human missense allele.
Small corneal diameter, the most consistently reported feature. Many reported corneas measure 10 to 10.5 mm, so a strict below-10 mm threshold would exclude over half of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Microcornea with myopic chorioretinal atrophy, telecanthus and posteriorly-rotated ears: a distinct clinical syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Horizontal corneal diameters ranged from 9.8 to 10.5 mm but anterior chambers were not shallow (2.66-3.01 mm).

evidence.snippet: Microcornea appears to be the only feature universally reported across patients; however even this is debatable given differences in definitions of microcornea and effects of aging

nodes.description: Chorioretinal atrophy, typically around the optic disc, and a generalised retinal dystrophy that is most often cone-rod in type, with severe rod and cone dysfunction on electroretinography in some patients. The degree of atrophy and dystrophy is not explained by myopia alone, which argues for a primary retinal defect rather than a consequence of axial elongation. In medaka, knockdown of the orthologue impairs photoreceptor function.

evidence.reference_title: The ADAMTS18 gene is responsible for autosomal recessive early onset severe retinal dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: In vivo gene knockdown performed in medaka fish confirmed both that the mutation has a pathogenic role and that the inactivation of this gene has a deleterious effect on photoreceptor cell function.

nodes.description: Bilateral rhegmatogenous retinal detachment in two patients from two families; one repaired eye went on to phthisis bulbi.

nodes.description: Correction of myopia and astigmatism with spectacles, with amblyopia and strabismus care and low-vision aids as needed. No disease-modifying treatment exists.

evidence.reference_title: ADAMTS18-related anterior segment dysgenesis mistaken as Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Cycloplegic refraction was -2.00 -1.25 x180 and -3.25 -2.00 x170, and glasses with this refraction were dispensed.

nodes.description: Regular monitoring of intraocular pressure, the iridocorneal angle and the retina, so that angle-closure or developmental glaucoma and retinal detachment are caught early. Glaucoma, cataract and rhegmatogenous retinal detachment are treated surgically as in other patients; detachment repair has had poor outcomes in some eyes.
